utterances.text: Would you agree with me to consider that the army was controlling the flux of civilians, the flow of civilians, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The flowing of population was controlled by the command of the corps or people from the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the last question, you said, that's what I understood, on page 42 line 18, page 43 that the headquarters of the brigade were located in the basement, that is, in nuclear shelters of these buildings. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The very last thing, sir: If I tell you that we have here a statement stating, and I am referring to P3726.1, a high representative of the UN forces saying that this tunnel had been opened the end of March, perhaps, beginning of April, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, this is not related to one of the questions. We have talked about digging trenches to the entrance of the tunnel. We have during the examination-in-chief and cross-examination, you had ample opportunity -- at the opening of the tunnel and this is beyond the scope of what you are allowed to ask to the witness at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic -- yes, Mr. Stamp

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There was just one question I had from something arising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Question from what?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From the Bench. Further re-examination by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, were civilians population in Dobrinja compelled by force to remain in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ISMET HADZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, this -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am saying this before the witness for courtesy. We said that we did not have time to look at the last two documents that were communicated -- that were handed over by the Prosecution yesterday or the day before. We were not able to look at it until now, so we are stating this with the reservation, the Defence is stating that if we discover things in these documents, can we be able to recall this witness? This is not certain, this is a reserve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you ask the right to reserve to ask to recall the witness if there is anything new in the documents that you just referred to. Yes. Mr. Hadzic, this concludes your testimony in this court. Thank you very much for having come to The Hague. A lot of questions were put to you both by the parties and by the Judges. You answered them and I would like to thank you for coming and answering the questions and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless there is a specific reason -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. If it is the case and the Defence recalls this witness, it would be good that he should be reminded that he should not speak to anyone about this. It could be within a week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether this could be within a week and it is at this moment rather hypothetical. Mr. Hadzic, the Defence has reserved the right to ask whether -- to ask the Bench to have you recalled for reasons not yet known at this moment. That would mean that you should not talk with anyone about your testimony at least not during the first week to come, since there is still a chance -- I am not saying that there is a probability, but it is a big chance or a small chance that you would be recalled. In the event if that would happen, then we would rather see you here without you having discussed your testimony with anyone. You understood that? Yes. Then again, thank you, and Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Hadzic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. But I was wondering if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we first have to deal with the documents. You are perfectly right. Since it is quite a number of documents, I should not have forgotten it. Madam Registrar could you please guide us through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3729, CD-rom; Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you have the wrong disk.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We might have the wrong disk. I think we are doing the list for Ewa Tabeau now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think, as a matter of fact, that this is the CD-rom that still waits to be tendered with the chart of the witness Philipps. Is that true, Madam Registrar? Or is it the data of -- what do we find on the CD-rom?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3732, map marked by witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to the map, and following a question that your Chamber asked, I was wondering whether we could perhaps, before the map is admitted, we would like to ask the Prosecution to give us the exact scales. I think that would help us to establish the right distances. I hope that the Prosecution is aware of the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this is something that all the parties could agree upon. The maps are maps from, I think, a particular one known as 7 Nima and for some purposes they are expanded, they are reduced. My understanding is an --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me be short. We have approximately six or seven maps with an exact scale. We have asked for it a several times. If you take a centimetre, and we all know how large this is, it is easy for everyone to establish the scale without any mistake and do whatever calculations you will have to do. I mean, discussing at length the scale of every single map while we can easily reconstruct it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may, with respect to the Exhibit, at the bottom of the Exhibit, the line that goes across, just above the names Hogan and Zaimovic, the lines are marked in areas of 100 metres between each square is a kilometre. I beg your pardon -- yes, each square is a kilometre and it is subdivided along the line in 100 metres. Regardless of how the maps are enlarged or reduced, that can assist in determining distances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would be of guidance then, Madam Registrar. So we don't need a specific scale, but we do know what the scale is, whether enlarged or not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D158, letter dated 23/01/1994, in B/C/S; D158.1, English translation; D159, letter dated 08/10/1992 in B/C/S; D159.1, English translation; D160, order dated 01/11/1992 by Ismet Hadzic, in B/C/S; D160.1 English translation; D161, order dated 01/11/1992 from Ismet Hadzic in B/C/S; D161.1, English translation; D162, intelligence report dated 01 October 1993 in B/C/S; D162.1, English translation, partial translation; D163, letter dated 5 December 1993 by Rasim Delic, in B/C/S; D163.1, English translation; D164, document in B/C/S, war diary 1993; D164.1, partial English translation; D165, letter dated 07 December 1993, problems of leadership and commanding in 5th Motorised Brigade for 1st Corps command; D165.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stamp, may I then -- your next witness will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We would respectfully object to the reception into evidence of D164.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is part of the book of Stjepan Siber, as far as I understand, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I can't recall the number of a statement that the witness had been shown or perhaps it was not tendered. In respect to D164, Mr. President, Your Honours, it is the Prosecution submission that a book by someone else is not probative, if the witness has not in any way accepted what it is saying. Neither is the statement by that person. It does not assist in the finding or resolving any of the issues that the Court is faced with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I am surprised. I thought that we spoke at length before this Chamber about a

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [redacted]. What is interesting, is that the commander of this witness declared certain things and what is more interesting, Mr. President, is that the communication between Mr. Stjepan Siber and this person responsible for the Dobrinja Brigade was not functioning. So this is a very important piece of evidence for the Defence in order to demonstrate that the chain of command at the very same time when we thought that they were perfectly established, very frequently were not functioning, were not operational. And if this was not in operation for the army of Sarajevo which has now been demonstrated it can also happen that it wasn't operational, it wasn't working for the VRS Army. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, perhaps, I don't know if we

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the second thing really is that the situation there was that the witness accepted and adopted the contents of the book. Here the witness says he doesn't know about what is said in the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained for two reasons: First of all, the comparison with another book that has been quoted is not a reason to accept this part of this book for the reason that that book reflected something the witness testified about, where in this case, the witness says that he doesn't know anything about it. The second reason is that the Defence makes the mistake that if this witness does not confirm what is in the book, that the line of command is not functioning well, that suggests that what is in the book is true. Of course, it may be true. The Chamber doesn't know. But if the Defence takes the position that it is true what is in this book, then the Prosecution should have an opportunity to test the reliability of the person that expressed his views in this book. Therefore, the objection is sustained and D164 will not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just to make sure that things are clear, the Defence believes, although it takes note of your position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not a position, it is a decision, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Of your decision. The Defence however believes and we have to say it, that our rights have been offended on the level of evidence. We need to say this at this very moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your next witness would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs. Recall of Dr. Kovacs. Before we start with the examination of Dr. Kovacs, I will tell you to what limits the examination of Dr. Kovacs may go. First, the Prosecution will have an opportunity to, if they want to, to examine Dr. Kovacs on, I would say, the history of his statement, if I may express it that way. I think everyone knows what I mean. So if there is any need to do that, the Prosecution may first do so. If necessary, the Chamber will put additional questions in this respect. Then the Defence is allowed to cross-examine the witness on every aspect that was not known to the parties at the conclusion of the previous examination of Dr. Kovacs. So that could include part of what I will call "the history" and certainly would include the last pages that have been added, that were in the last version of the report we received and that were not in the previous report that was distributed. So that is the order of the examination of Dr. Kovacs. Mr. Usher, could you please -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, before Mr. Kovacs enters the witness box, the Defence would like to underscore that the Defence will not examine this witness, except that they were forced to do this, and I have to explain, that this document was never submitted to the Defence with the respect of the deadlines, with the respect of a rule 94 and others. So the examination of this witness is happening under these circumstances. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that I would rather not talk about being "forced," but at least I can imagine that the Defence is not quite happy with the situation it is in and I think that the Chamber has already expressed that it was not very happy with what happened in respect of Dr. Kovacs's report. On the other hand, the Chamber has carefully looked at the contents, especially of the added or at least to the last pages of the final report of the Dr. Kovacs and is of the opinion that the contents is such that the Defence should be able to cross-examine the witness on these parts of the report. But I -- the Chamber has taken notes of the observation the Defence just made. Would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, can you hear me in a language, even if it is with the help of the interpreter, in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since it has been quite some time, I would rather ask you to make again the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your previous testimony. So the text of that solemn declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please be seated. May I ask you to remain standing. I took the wrong order because I would have had to ask you to make a solemn declaration first. Therefore, I invite you to make a solemn declaration as an interpreter and would you -- may I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will interpret faithfully and impartially and with full respect for the duty of the confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to confirm that the interpretation that you have done until now, has been done in a similar spirit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With your leave, Mr. President, could the witness be handed document Exhibit P3725 and P37251.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, may I ask the interpreter whether she is Maria Bolgar?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And also, Mr. President, he has been shown already P3725A.1 and P3725A. I will ask for P3725. Can he also be shown that one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have P3725A.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. The original document which was received in evidence on the previous occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I believe they're recalling a copy, in the meantime, may I ask the Doctor some questions until one is located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes you may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, you had been asked to prepare a report in respect of artillery matters for the purposes of this case, had you not?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you prepare a draft report sometime in February of this year?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We call that "working copy."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And subsequent to that, in April of this year, did you prepare a final copy of that report, of your report?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you prepare it in the Hungarian language?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Both were prepared in the Hungarian language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The final one which you prepared, did you fax a copy of that to the relevant officials of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With the assistance of Mr. Usher, could he be shown P3725A. It is with him now. He has it already. Could you indicate to him which one is P3725, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at that document, and tell us if this is the report you prepared in your own language?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the one I prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the last page of it, it is dated the 30th of April, 2002?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have signed it?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now have a look at the document marked P3725A.1. Could you look at page 30 of that document.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And line 22 from the top of that page, could you find that line, please. Do you see a sentence there beginning: "I have given the answers"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I see the sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you peruse from that sentence to the end of the document, approximately one to two pages? Could you look at, check and read from that sentence to the end of the document and tell us if that is a translation into English of the Hungarian text of the document, of the 30th of April 2002.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I could do that, if I see it. Close to two pages, my knowledge of the English language does not enable me to go through it very quickly. I would need to put the two text beside each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may compare the two texts.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if the witness says that he is not, due to his limited knowledge of the English language, if he is saying that he cannot do it, perhaps it would be good to ask him to read his report in his original language and then we may come closer to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It could be done that way too. But he did say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness did not say that he could not do it --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is just a matter of time. Perhaps, Mr. Stamp, we could do that during the break, although, I am aware that it is not nice for the witness to read the two documents, but to apply the same procedure as we did before, that in the presence of the Registrar, that the witness gets the time or in the presence of one of the legal officers, that the witness gets the time to compare whether his original report and the English translation, whether that is there in both the documents. And the parties of course may remain for the time the witness would need for that in the courtroom so that they can see that he is not consulting everyone -- anyone. If we do it this way we are sure that he takes the time he needs and that we will have a reliable answer to your last question. Dr. Kovacs, may I ask you to read this part of the document. You say you couldn't do it quickly. Just take your time. I would like to ask you to remain in this courtroom so that everyone can see that you are consulting no one while performing this task. When you are ready, please tell the Officer of the Court that is present, that you are ready. If there is any time left, of course, there is a break for you as well. And during the break, you are supposed not to speak with anyone about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I make one inquiry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This would not -- you are not supposed to talk with the interpreter about your testimony, but if you would need the assistance of the interpreter for the comparison, you can ask her assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That was my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your request. We will then adjourn until 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, I feel sorry for you that we had a break and you had not. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the transcript, it would be good to say that we have our expert who is sitting with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Welcome in the courtroom. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should indicate one thing to you first. The Chamber decided that since document P3725 was filed it would not have to be admitted into evidence and not to be tendered anymore. Therefore, the Registrar has retrieved the filed copy, so if you would use it, it is not an exhibit, but it is a filed report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I perhaps would not use it, but I thought it should be available here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is there if you need it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, having had an opportunity to peruse the translation from where I showed you, that is, line 22 down from the top of page 30 to the end of the document, in English.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I did examine the section you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that a true and accurate translation into English of the Hungarian text of your report?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: The text in question matches the Hungarian text, but on three accounts, I have some corrections or additions to the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you do so?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: On line 6 of page 31, in the beginning of the line, there is the phrase "acoustic locaters." The correct term is, "sound locaters." One line lower, the translation lacks one word. The correct phrase would be "gun and mortar of the platoon."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you go on, you were, in respect to that second correction, you would insert the words "and mortar" between the word "gun" and "of"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Of course, what I described in that sentence are true for guns and for mortars. If we add "and mortar" then it matches my Hungarian text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now move on to the third one.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: In line 12 of page 31, there is the third mistake. It now reads, "gun or battery," and the correct version would be "gun or mortar." I would like to make this change, because what is written there is true for guns or mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything else you would like to change, or is that it?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness, because at this moment, there are no further clarifications to be asked by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to be specific, yes and no. The Defence is not ready, with the reserves that we have stated, but the Defence will go on with the cross-examination. If you permit me, I would like to begin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacs, on two to two and a half pages of the text you made three corrections. The rest seems to reflect your thoughts. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: The remainder of the text does not contain anything to be corrected, and basically, matches the Hungarian version written by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the permission of the Bench, I would like to show you a document which will be document D166. Your Honour, I have to specify the following, and I am doing that in order not to lead the witness to a mistake. The document that you will see is simply a masked copy of the last page of the document we received before the incident and it is simply because we overburdened him perhaps while we were working, so I would not like to lead the witness to commit some kind of a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of the Hungarian report?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is about the first, faulty version that we received from the Prosecution, the one that has only 29 pages, and the one that I asked for during the questioning. And I can present that to the Bench so that you can establish that the copy of the document that I am providing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am asking you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Serves only to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- For the following reason. The report that has been submitted is the final version of the report, not any previous draft report or working report. I would like you to keep that clearly in mind and indicate, since, if this is what the witness called the "working report," you will be very limited in questioning him about it and not asking him whether he agrees with certain elements which he might have left behind in the final report. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. I would like the witness to read to us four sentences that have been provided to him, four sentences from his working report so that these sentences could be translated into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please read in your own language these four lines. I mean, read aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "All commanders have to know the effect of a projectile hitting the target or its vicinity and thus must be able to decide whether the destruction and devastation zone is outside the boundary that may not be crossed by the military because of the possible civilian casualties. It is called murder" -- no, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's error. "Because of the possible civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there has been a mistake in the English booth. I think that it is quite clear that the word, "it is called murder" is not mentioned and that this witness did not state that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the interpretation now of these lines of a report which is not submitted to the Chamber is that the line reads: "Civil casualties," and not "murder".

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely. But I would like the witness to confirm for us the essence of this translation error. For the English booth, just for the witness to simply confirm the translation that was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that this report, dating -- is it true that this report is dated February 2002?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would like to know which report you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am speaking about the report that you called, "the working report" or "the working copy.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Your question is, if these four lines are in the working copy? Could you specify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is: Is it true that what you have just read is from your report from February 2002?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: It is similar to what I had in my report of February 2002, but I could only confirm this definitely if I would have my working copy of February to compare it to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have that copy with you?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't have that copy with me. The only thing in front of me is the copy from April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if the Registrar has this first, faulty report that I received. If not, I can provide our own text but, unfortunately, it is marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... tendered into evidence. It has been provided to you. Unfortunately --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I then show our text to the witness so that he can identify it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you show the relevant page, if you ask the usher to show the relevant page and ask the witness whether he now can confirm that this was part of his text.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please don't pay any attention to the handwritten remarks. Can you confirm that this is the text that you have written?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: If I am correct, the last page, page 29 of this report, I don't see any date or signature by myself on this page. So I cannot confirm this with my -- consciously, with my conscience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, take your time, and you should be able to know whether this is your report or this is a report from some other source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that it is the position of the Defence that it comes from the same report. The Prosecution has a copy of that report, so there is agreement on that. Would you please go to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are talking about the credibility of this witness, this witness is hesitating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... what he experienced. It is your position that these four lines appear in his original Hungarian report. The Prosecution agrees, so please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you wrote, in the final version of your report, some additional words claiming that it is "murder". In relation to this expert report, what happened between the 18th of February 2002 until the 13th -- until the 30th of April 2002, so that you suddenly added these words to your report, "it is called murder." So this is your report?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, the usher could return the first document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the period you are referring to, between February and April 2002, I worked through a major part of the material. As I mentioned before, the previous version was a version -- working copy, and working through this text had an improvement as its aim. So this -- this is what happened in those two months that I had the material with me and I was working on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, did you necessarily get in touch with anyone between the 18th of February and the 30th of April, 2002? When I am talking about "persons" I am thinking of people from the Office of the Prosecution, Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I understand your question. And in the time you are referring to, I received questions referring to what subjects should be more expressly indicated to achieve a better understanding. I also made some improvements or corrections on my own initiative, and the two factors resulted in the new material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And now, in relation to this excerpt that we are particularly interested in, did you discuss that with the Prosecution and did you receive questions, as you called them?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I have received a number of questions from the Prosecution and they mainly had to do with the structure of my text, on the one hand, and also some of them were questions that had to do with the use of cannons and artillery so as to better understand the use of these weapons for the layman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, Dr. Kovacs. The question is quite clear, whether on these words, that is, "civilian casualties" in one version and "murder" in the second version, which is a stronger language, whether you received any suggestions by the Prosecution to change that language. That is the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when you are talking about these expressions and you are talking about the context, I did not make these changes under pressure, in any way whatsoever. I changed it on my own accord.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether there was any questions specifically on this part, this wording of the report, not whether you were under pressure to change it. You might have fully agreed when you changed it if there were questions about it. The question simply is: Were there any questions on this specific part of the report or any suggestion? Is this a specific issue you discussed, in whatever way, with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand your question very well, Your Honour. And my answer is a definite no. I have not received any question whatsoever regarding this particular issue. There was no question referring to this among the ones I have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And no suggestions either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there were no suggestions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Expert, you are confirming that the changes you made came from your own initiative. You decided on your own initiative to add this as "murder"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, please talk about the Hungarian version because I can only take full responsibility for the Hungarian text. And I think that the Hungarian version which I added in April --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Expert, we have to interrupt you. We know that there are two texts that are very different. I am asking you if it is your own initiative to decide to add these words that you know that mean "this is murder, yes or no? Without paraphrasing.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: In the expert text, every word that you find was put there, was written down, by me, of my own accord.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question with a yes or no, if you can. So it was your own initiative that lead you, following the 18th of February, to add these words, these additional words?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, so the rest of the report hasn't changed, in essence. What caused this change on your side, on your par?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think that this is a considerable change, a discrepancy, as compared to the reality because there have been different changes of meaning. It is not simply the words that have changed. I think there are some essential facts that have been modified. And this is how you are supposed to read my text. It is not two or three words that have changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are saying to me that the two texts between the 18th of February and the 30th of April, are that different, are actually different in essence?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say that the copy dated February 2002 is a working copy. I made a number of changes in that particular text. And in April, I drew up my final version and I did not state anything else apart from this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I think we understand that there are two different documents, one working copy and one final copy. Now, my question is, please, these two texts, are they that different in essence, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would like to ask you just what exactly you mean by "to this extent" in your question? Yes, there are differences, there are differences between the two texts, but they are not radical changes, but are certain stylistic differences and a number of things that I have added, completed my text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, we will then agree to say that in fact these two texts are not fundamentally different, they are not different in their essence, then?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I am going to repeat myself. We are talking about two different materials. The first one is a working document. The second one is the final version of my text. And now to express the difference in percentages between the two versions, well, I couldn't do this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I again interfere. Dr. Kovacs, by mistake your earlier report was given to the Defence, and they have compared your working report with the final report. There seem to be not major changes in view. The Defence has drawn the attention of the Chamber to those changes that appear in your final text compared the earlier text. What the Defence wants to know is what makes you choose the far stronger wordings "murder," where your earlier report used the expression "civil casualties." That is the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Thank you very much for the question. And, Your Honour, I am not -- I am not a specialist in legal matters and I am sure you are aware of this. And so when I used the word "murder," I did not use it in the legal sense, and of course, I didn't think of this when I was writing my text. It has no legal implications and I am sure that in your terminology, this might mean something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you changed the wording. What did you make feel not satisfied with the words "civil casualties"? Why did you want to change the wording and then subsequently you have chosen the word, "murder"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have liked to express in some way that there is a difference between civilian casualties that I brought about accidentally and civilian casualties brought about on purpose. And that is what I wanted to indicate and perhaps from the legal point of view, I did not use the proper terminology. But I had the feeling that perhaps this way, I could express the view that possibly there was an intention behind this act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well, that you felt that the wording "civil casualties" would be more appropriate for just accidental civilian people dying, while you were of the opinion that the situation you described came closer to a situation where you should blame the person for the casualties. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is a shade of meaning. There is a difference. There is a slight difference between the two. I think that when you talk about civil casualties, this is something that can happen when you destroy a military target without any intention to bring it about. But at the same time, you can also have civil casualties intentionally. And I wanted to show the difference and perhaps I had not chosen the proper expression, did not use the right sentence, but that was my idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thank you, Witness, for the clarifications. We are going to continue now. So, you will agree with me that the expression that you have used, whatever was its meaning, it is though hypothetical, since you were not able to know, practically speaking, if such-and-such a person did have an element of intent in order to cause a particular result? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Of course. I agree, because I wasn't present and I didn't want to express the intent by saying this, I just wanted to indicate a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed. Therefore, we will agree that the term of "murder" that you used in your report, this is purely theoretical and hypothetical, based on this?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will proceed very briefly on another question, another point, Mr. President, with the reserves that I have already expressed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said on page 30 of the translation of your expert report, also known as the "final version that you tried, you attempted to bring answers to -- and I am now going to quote the words used in English then: [In English] "Questions and assumptions drawn up by the MAT." First question, could you please remind us what do you mean by "MAT"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is an abbreviation mean the Military Analysis Team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, this is the Prosecution? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't really know exactly the links between the Prosecution and the Military Analysis Team. This is why I put it down as it is, because that was the way the question was put to me. So I am referring to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what do you mean by using the term "assumptions"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Assumptions refer to possibilities that might have -- things that might have happened, one or two of them might have happened, but they are not referring to concrete events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, am I to conclude that the Prosecution or the "MAT" had given you a number of such assumptions; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: The Military Analysis Team, in general, meant that we were looking at questions and possibilities in general and we examined them together, jointly, and I tried to help them from -- with my expertise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But this data, this assumption, was given do you by the Prosecution, were they not?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. No. I am referring to something else. I am referring to something that we have dealt together, it is a computation of probabilities, if you like, and everything element of this computation is based on suppositions and of course what we are studying is the first shell, the first fire and the precision of the first fire, so that there is -- I can't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, another two questions, Witness. Who and who with did you work?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: On behalf of the Military Analysis Team, there was a group and at the same time, we also had a Hungarian group, a Hungarian team comprising a number of specialists and I was a member of that particular group. And we discussed various questions, theoretical questions, related to the artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. My question was: And where? And where did you work?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: You wanted to know where exactly these questions were asked, geographically speaking?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you work? Yes, geographically speaking.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: There were two meetings between the two groups. And this group of question that we were discussing and studying in the year 2000, was working in Budapest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since there is a group, it seems to be in Budapest, could you perhaps tell us some names of experts who had worked with you?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, that took place in the fall of the year 2000, so I don't really remember any specific name. I was a member of the group, but I couldn't give you any names, specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were a member of a group of experts and you cannot give me names of people, experts, that you worked with in Budapest, Hungary or you do not wish to do that?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: You understood me correctly, I cannot give you the names; I just can't remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you be able to find these names in that way, perhaps you can come back with these names.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't think I would be able to give you the names because I didn't know these people before. I only met them once and I don't think I have kept their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you worked with a group of experts, you only saw them once, you don't know how to find them again, and you don't know their names; is that what I am to understand from your answer?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you correctly and you understood what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these experts, were they men or women?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, if you would give it a good effort, do you think someone must have constituted this group, someone has invited you, and I take it other members of the group as well? Would you be able to reconstruct those persons of whom the group consisted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would give it a good effort, whether you could find the names of those who took part in that group, and I suggested to you that someone was must have called the members of the group together and must have invited you, I take it, to participate in that group. So perhaps that person would still know the names of the other members of the group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is quite probable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there anything else you would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes, but we are going to let the witness think about it overnight and then we are going to ask more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It depends, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You left the area of what you could have not have asked the witness at the previous occasion, that whether he worked together with others by preparing his report, was a question that could have perfectly put to the witness. The reason why I intervened is that I wondered whether that would be the last answer of the witness on what he could or could not. But, are there any other issues concerning --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- [Previous translation continues]... Two pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. That is the reason why I believe that in order not to make it difficult for anyone, particularly not difficult for the witness, perhaps we could do it tomorrow morning as early possible, that is the first hours of the hearing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first hours would be quite a lot of time for two pages, but let me just confer with the other members of the Chamber. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it is possible that we can complete today, I respectfully ask that we try to do so. I think that there are huge difficulties with this witness. He has pressing personal matters which he had to leave to come here. And also we have only booked the Hungarian interpreters for today and I am not sure if they will be available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, that last part -- well, let me confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters suggest to the President that the Hungarian interpreters can stay tomorrow and that most people do not want to work after 7.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware of that and as I already expressed the argument of the "not being available any more" of the Hungarian interpreter would certainly not be the reason for the decision the Chamber would first like to make. But we'd first ask the interpreters booth we would like the continue for not more and strictly 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Hungarian interpreters are able to stay on until tomorrow. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not a matter of the interpreters. It is for other reasons that we would like to conclude. So it is not for the interpreters that we continue, but for other reasons. Would the interpreters --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have 15 minutes exactly, not more, to put all the questions to the witness you would like to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please give me now the names, all the names of the people that you remember from that group. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: As I mentioned before, sir, I don't remember the names from this group. So I couldn't give them to you now, and I couldn't give them to you 15 minutes hence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember one of the names or two of the names? Please give the names that you would remember, even if it would not be all of the group at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Your Honour, I can't give you a correct answer just now. That happened two years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, were these people men or women?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Civilian or military?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Everybody was wearing civilian clothes, so I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Young or old?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I am going on to another line of questioning. How long did this committee work until? Or this commission?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would like to correct your question, if you don't mind. It was not a committee. I don't know the exact definition, but in my opinion, it was an ad hoc group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, how long did the group work together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions. We were discussing a number of questions, not concrete questions, general issues, and it only took a few hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, until which date, which day, which year, did this group work? If you don't know it, just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it true that this group was already created in the year 2000; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: It was in the year 2000 that the questions cropped up and these are the questions I am referring to now. That's all I can say --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question is following: Can you please answer with a yes or no if possible, do you know if this group was established in the year 2000; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: This discussion took place in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So this group did this group see the draft of the conclusion, of the findings of the report?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the expert opinion which is in front of me on the table?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about what you called, Witness, your working document. Did they see it or not?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, sir. That's what I stated before. It is my own work. I produced it, nobody in the whole world saw it or commented on it from the expert point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I told you before that you were far away from the last two pages and from what you could not have asked the witness before. Would you please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I am just going to come back to one of the pages that we have recently discovered. And you stated the following on page 31, end of the second paragraph, more or less, that the error of firing, what I conclude to be the error of firing was about 200 to 400 metres. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps the question may be more easily comprehended by the witness if the document is quoted from precisely, the relevant passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, I will quote. I will quote. [In English] "Of the first shot are specified for a point located 200, 400 metres from the target in the opposite direction."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You found the passage, Dr. Kovacs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour, I have found this passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Expert, that therefore there is an admissible error of about 400 metres; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I am terribly sorry. I cannot really answer this question because the whole text is not referring to what you are asking me about. Because this is not a question of a mistake. The 200 to 400 metres is not a question of mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Withdraw the word "mistake." Is there a margin of firing which could be between 200 and 400 metres?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, this is not the question. This is not what I am talking about in my text. In this particular sentence what I am saying is the following: That there is a possibility, if you have your own forces that happen to be in that particular area, then they would not start firing. There is a firing range and they would not start firing at the target, but at a certain point, a certain object which might be 200 or 400 metres away from that particular target, where there can be no casualties. That is what I am talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. By saying this, you are saying that there is a security margin of about 2 to 400 metres?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It is not a safety limit. It is a little more than that. It is more than a level of a safety limit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So what is it, in a nutshell?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is a little more than a safety zone, if you like. And this is precisely so as to protect our own forces against undesired damage, undesirable damage, and this is the way you use artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Whatever name we give it, this is a margin in order to protect, with the purpose of protecting one's own forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. It can mean that, in a certain way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So it could be like a security margin, more or less?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be, but this is not what it is. There is a difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Very well. Now this quasi-margin of safety or of security, Witness, doesn't it mean that when there is firing, there is also a risk of error which corresponds precisely to the margin or the quasi-margin of security; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: There is a possibility of making a mistake, and of course it can take place at any point in time whatsoever and this is precisely why you have this distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The very last question in this time that is given to me: Is it correct, Mr. Expert, that the deviations are not simply in the axis but they can also deviate from the axis, that is, not only in depth, but also laterally, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Naturally, there could be a lateral deviation as well, but a deviation in depth, in general, is greater than a deviation sideways.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will stop here for the obvious reasons. The Defence is hereby stating the reservation that we may have to recall this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Stamp, you insisted on the witness to be excused. May I take it that there are no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are just a couple and they will be asked by Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cannot ask at 7.00 for the witness to be excused and ask the interpreters, who clearly said to us that they prefer not to work after 7.00 and of course they have their responsibilities as well. Let me just do the following. You get one minute that was saved by the Defence to put the most important question you would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I ask those questions, I can assure you that they only relate to one topic, which is the so-called group and I think the reason will become obvious as to why we need to ask those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One or two questions and it is upon your request that we continued and not on the request of anyone else. Yes, please. Re-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was all the Lieutenant-Colonel Bela Komka and Lieutenant-Colonel Antal Herdics and some military aides, the individuals present with you at the meeting in late 2000 at the Hague and myself?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Bela Komka is an artillery officer. He might have been there, in the year 2000, he might have been there. Would you repeat the other name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel A-N-T-A-L H-E-R-D-I-C-S and some military aides and myself.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you repeat once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A-N-T-A-L H-E-R-D-I-C-S, and some military aides, Hungarian acting as translators and myself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Herdics, yes, he is also an artillery officer. I don't remember exactly whether he was there or not, but I can imagine he might have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And military aides acting as interpreters and myself?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that there were interpreters and that is how we were working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember me being there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember me being there as well?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: You mean in 2000?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Second question, when were you first asked to do a report, in other words to be an expert witness, approximately?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Recalled]
utterances.text: In 2002, at the beginning of 2002, a few weeks prior to my February text.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the absence of the Hungarian interpreter -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, since there are no questions from the bench, this concludes your second testimony in this court. I thank you for coming back to The Hague and wish you a safe journey home. We adjourn until tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00, but not after I have specifically thanked the interpreters for their great flexibility. I know that I am building up a bad reputation. I apologise for that. And we will be in Courtroom I tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
